title: Build the TaskFlow Web Shell
goal: Turn the React mental model into a real Next.js App Router application with deliberate server/client boundaries.
steps: Create the Next.js app and inspect every generated top-level file before editing.
Build the root layout and a simple application shell.
Add `/tasks` and `/tasks/[id]` routes and navigate using `Link`.
Keep the task list page server-side and fetch server data there.
Create a small Client Component for filtering or dialog state instead of marking the whole page client-side.
Add `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, and `not-found.tsx` and reproduce each state deliberately.
Separate server-only and public environment variables.
Run the production build and fix every warning/error before moving on.
evidence: A clean Git diff or file-tree change
Browser, HTTP, database, test, container, or CI evidence that proves the behavior
One deliberate failure, the evidence you used, and the root-cause fix
A short explanation of why the final responsibility lives in the chosen layer
completion: I can reproduce one key part without the walkthrough.
I can explain one trade-off I deliberately chose.
I can show one failure that my tests, constraints, or runbook now protects against.
